title: Statistics: Variance, Standard Deviation, Ogives and Skewed Data
seo_title: Grade 11 Statistics Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Histograms, frequency polygons, ogives (cumulative frequency curves); variance and standard deviation of ungrouped data; symmetric and skewed data; identification of outliers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 statistics worksheets: variance, standard deviation, ogives, grouped data and skewed data. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Adding to every value does not change σ.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Variance: σ² = Σ(x − x̄)²n. Standard deviation σ is the square root of the variance.
  • Adding a number to every value does not change σ; multiplying every value by k multiplies σ by k.
  • An ogive is a cumulative frequency graph: read the median at n/2 and the quartiles at n/4 and 3n/4.
  • Symmetric data: mean ≈ median. Skewed data: the mean is pulled towards the tail.

Examples

Example

2; 4; 6; 8

x̄ = 5

σ² = (9 + 1 + 1 + 9) ÷ 4 = 5

Answer: σ ≈ 2,24

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not squaringSquare each deviation.
No square rootσ is the root of the variance.
The ogiveRead at n/2 for the median.

items.q: Values with mean 69 and standard deviation 2 are each multiplied by 3 and then increased by 5. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Mean: 69 × 3 + 5 = 212. SD: only the multiplication matters, 2 × 3 = 6. mean 212, SD 6.

items.q: A set of marks has mean 56 and standard deviation 6. Every mark is increased by 10. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
items.e: Adding the same amount for every value moves the mean by 10 but does not change the spread: mean 66, SD 6.
